text:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: Alert fired: routing-service.p99_latency >= 1200ms in eu-west & ap-south. Pager: #incident-4772.

Alex M: taking handoff for the pager, thread_ts=3156789012. Quick summary: new smart-routing policy (rollout-2026-03) seems to cause a routing loop between the regional proxy and the cost-aware fallback. Symptoms: p99 token latency spike, some 429 throttles for Dedicated customers in eu-west/ap-south. No full outage but customer-facing degradations.

Cheng L: confirmed. Seeing increased retry rates and duplicate request IDs in traces. Spike started ~20m after rollout. Primary cluster (eu-west-a) shows elevated connection churn to model variants.

Maya R: I've paused active canaries (k8s label remove) and attached a rate-limiter temp rule to reduce traffic to the new route. That reduced error rates but latency still high for tail.

Alex M: actions so far: 1) paused canaries 2) applied per-route rate-shedding rule 3) enabled fallback to model-variant small-llama for top 5 affected customers.

OpsBot: Command executed: `routingctl rollback policy rollout-2026-03 --scope=eu-west,ap-south` -> started.

Sam K: logs from proxy show this pattern: `WARN route-loop detected src=proxy-12 dest=router-3 attempts=6` and `TRACE request=abcd123 retry=5`. Looks like our compatibility check for variant-mapping returned null in one path, triggering fallback that is itself routed back through the new policy.

Nora S: runbook pointer — see runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/smart-routing (section "rollback and fallback") and the short mitigation play: use `routingctl set-fallback-mode conservative` then `routingctl drain-policy rollout-2026-03`.

Cheng L: rollback is in progress per OpsBot, watching metrics. Canary pause + rate-shed gave immediate <10% reduction in 429s, but p99 still 800-1200ms in eu-west. Might take a few minutes for caches and KV warm-up.

Alex M: customer impact: A subset of Dedicated customers in eu-west/ap-south saw increased latencies and some 429s for high-throughput routes. No data loss. I've notified support and AMs with the incident stub.

Maya R: open tasks for next shift: 1) confirm full rollback completion and diff of routing config, 2) run model-variant compatibility probe across regions (`/ops/probes/variant-compat`), 3) collect 5 sample traces for each affected customer and attach to the incident.

Sam K: tip — if you need to reproduce locally, use this curl to force the path:```bash
curl -H 'X-Routing-Policy: rollout-2026-03' -d '{"input":"test"}' https://proxy.eu-west.internal/v1/generate
```

Oncall Bot: Pager update posted to #incident-4772. Next escalation in 15m if errors persist.

Alex M: Handoff notes for whoever picks this up: I'm primary until 08:00 UTC. Cheng will be secondary tonight. Brevity checklist: - If rollback completes and p99 < 300ms for 10m, we can close pager. - If 429s persist for >30m after rollback, escalate to infra oncall (tag @infra-lead) and consider traffic-shift to us-west.

Cheng L: Outstanding unknowns: Does the policy interact with our KV cache warmup order? We saw a sequence where fallback lookups happen before prefix cache is ready. If that's true, we might need a small startup delay or a pre-warm.

Maya R: I've left the commands I used pinned in the incident thread and uploaded `routing-rollback.log` to the incident channel. Also flagged the rollout owner (@deploy-team) for a postmortem.

Alex M: Coverage/shift handoff: Cheng you're now primary from 08:00 UTC -> 16:00 UTC. Maya will be reachable for escalation. If primary/secondary both are busy, ping Sam.

Cheng L: ACK. I'll watch dashboards (SLO/routing/trace-sampler) and reply on #incident-4772. My immediate next steps: 1) validate rollback diff 2) confirm no residual route entries via `routingctl list --stale` 3) collect traces and mark as evidence.

Nora S: reminder: update the status page draft if we have >30% customer-impacting requests. I started a template in #incidents-drafts.

Alex M: leaving the bridge. If anything spikes, ring the pager or @channel here. :white_check_mark:

OpsBot: Action completed: `routingctl rollback policy rollout-2026-03` -> success (deploy-id: rollback-2026-03-001). Metrics back to baseline in ap-south; eu-west p99 trending down.

Cheng L: will keep monitoring. If p99 stabilizes under 300ms for 15m and 429s <1%, I'll mark pager resolved and post final notes.

Sam K: also recommend we add a post-rollback probe to CI that simulates high-concurrency requests to catch routing loops during future canaries.

Alex M: thanks team. Handoff complete.
